cards.title: Private PAC sample complexity from VC and Littlestone dimensions
cards.formal: Do there exist universal integers \(A,k\ge1\) such that every nonempty finite Boolean concept class \(\mathcal C\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\) on a nonempty finite domain \(\mathcal X\), with \(v=\operatorname{VC}(\mathcal C)\ge1\) and \(d=\operatorname{LD}(\mathcal C)\ge1\), has a positive integer sample size \[m\le A\bigl(1+v+\log^{*}d\bigr)^{k}\] and a possibly improper learner \(L\) that is \((1,1/(100m^{2}))\)-differentially private and realizes the following PAC guarantee? For every distribution \(D\) on \(\mathcal X\) and every target \(h^{*}\in\mathcal C\), when \(L\) receives \(m\) independent samples \((x_i,h^{*}(x_i))\) with \(x_i\sim D\), its output \(\widehat h\) satisfies \[\Pr\!\left[\Pr_{x\sim D}[\widehat h(x)\ne h^{*}(x)]\le1/10\right]\ge9/10.\] The same \(m,L\) must work for all \(D,h^{*}\) for the chosen class. Their choice can depend on the complete class, but \(A,k\) cannot. Computation is unrestricted. This is the previously selected concrete polynomial-overhead version of the source question; the constant accuracy, confidence and sample-dependent privacy parameters are editorial specifications, not parameter values asserted in the source.
cards.definitions: A concept is a binary function; the learner knows \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal C\). The VC dimension \(v\) is the largest cardinality of a subset \(S\subseteq\mathcal X\) on which the restrictions of \(\mathcal C\) realize every binary labeling. A complete binary tree of depth \(r\) has an instance point at each internal node and its two outgoing edges labeled 0 and 1. It is shattered by \(\mathcal C\) if every root-to-leaf edge-label sequence is produced by one fixed concept on that path's instance points. The Littlestone dimension \(d\) is the greatest shattered depth. For \(z\ge1\), \(\log^{*}z\) is the least number of successive base-two logarithms needed to obtain a value at most one; in particular \(\log^{*}1=0\). The dimension-zero case is excluded only to avoid a logarithm convention: on a fixed nonempty domain such a class contains a single distinct concept and has a data-independent exact predictor. A learner is an arbitrary probability kernel from \((\mathcal X\times\{0,1\})^m\) to the finite set \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\). It need not return a member of \(\mathcal C\). For every pair of labeled sample lists \(S,S'\) differing at one position and every subset \(E\) of output hypotheses, require \[\Pr[L(S)\in E]\le e\Pr[L(S')\in E]+1/(100m^{2}).\] Privacy holds even on samples not realizable by the class. The sample size is chosen before the target and distribution; the probability in the PAC guarantee includes both independently drawn examples and the learner's randomness. There are no runtime or representation bounds, and no uniform program across classes is required. The integer-power bound is equivalent to an unspecified universal polynomial in \(1+v\) and \(1+\log^{*}d\). A finite class on an arbitrary domain can be reduced to the finite domain of distinct label vectors \((h(x))_{h\in\mathcal C}\), of which there are at most \(2^{|\mathcal C|}\); both dimensions and these unrestricted learning/privacy requirements are preserved. Thus the finite-domain convention introduces no additional sample-complexity restriction on finite classes.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a Lean-checked proof of the universal polynomial bound or its logical negation under the exact privacy and PAC conventions above. A positive answer must supply, for every class, a sample size and private learner satisfying the guarantee simultaneously for all targets and distributions. A negative answer must show that for every proposed pair of universal integers \(A,k\), some finite class admits no such learner at any positive integer sample size within the proposed bound. Computational lower bounds, proper-learning obstructions that disappear for improper learners, or a result only for one fixed VC dimension do not refute the statement.

cards.title: Optimal error for pure-DP continual counting
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors as \(T\to \infty , E(T)=\inf _{M} \max _{x\in \{0,1\}^{T}} E_{Y\sim M_{x}}[\max _{1\le t\le T}|Y_{t}- \sum_{i=1}^{t} x_{i}|]\), where the infimum is over all causal \((1/2,0)\)-differentially private mechanisms defined below.
cards.definitions: For an integer \(T\ge 2, a\) mechanism is a family of Borel probability distributions \(M_{x}\) on \(\mathbb{R} ^{T}\), one for each binary stream \(x\in \{0,1\}^{T}\). Its output \(Y_{t}\) is released immediately after observing \(x_{t}\). Causality means that whenever x and \(x'\) have the same first t bits, the marginal distributions of \((Y_{1},\ldots ,Y_{t})\) under \(M_{x}\) and \(M_{x}'\) are equal. The horizon T is known before the first output. Streams are fixed inputs, not adaptively chosen in response to outputs. Neighbors differ in exactly one bit, and pure privacy requires \(M_{x}(S)\le \exp (1/2)M_{x}' (S)\) for every pair of neighbors and every Borel \(S\subseteq \mathbb{R} ^{T}\). This protects the entire joint transcript, with no additive failure allowance. There is no restriction on computation, memory, real precision, output integrality or monotonicity; internal randomness may be correlated across times. A different family of probability distributions may be chosen for each T. The maximum over streams is outside the expectation; the maximum over time is inside it. The infimum is used without assuming attainment. \(E(T)\) is finite, for example because a data-independent all-zero transcript has error at most T. All logarithms in asymptotic comparisons may use any fixed base greater than one.
cards.answer_criterion: Determine an asymptotic rate \(g(T)\) and prove constants \(c,C>0\) and \(T_{0}\) such that \(c g(T)\le E(T)\le C g(T)\) for every \(T\ge T_{0}\). The upper guarantee must be achievable by permitted causal pure-private mechanisms, and the lower guarantee must cover all such mechanisms. Constants may not depend on T. The expected maximum absolute-error criterion must be the same on both sides.

cards.title: Finite-domain promise CSP dichotomy
cards.formal: For every fixed pair of finite relational structures \(A,B\) of the same finite signature, with nonempty domains and a homomorphism \(A\to B\), is the decision promise problem \(\operatorname{PCSP}(A,B)\) either solvable by a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm or NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one promise reductions? Its yes instances are the finite structures \(I\) with \(I\to A\); its no instances are those with \(I\not\to B\). The quantifier ranges over all finite signatures and template pairs. The algorithm or hardness reduction, including its polynomial bound, may depend on the fixed pair.
cards.definitions:
A signature is an ordered finite list \(R_1,\ldots,R_s\), where \(s\geq0\) and each symbol has a fixed positive integer arity \(r_i\). A finite structure \(D\) for this signature has a finite domain and relations \(R_i^D\subseteq D^{r_i}\). The templates have domains \(A=\{1,\ldots,a\}\), \(B=\{1,\ldots,b\}\) for positive integers \(a,b\); their relation tables are fixed, not part of the varying input. Different template domains are allowed. For two structures of the same signature, a homomorphism \(h:D\to E\) is a map of domains satisfying
\[\forall i\;\forall(v_1,\ldots,v_{r_i})\in R_i^D:\ (h(v_1),\ldots,h(v_{r_i}))\in R_i^E.\]
Write \(D\to E\) if such a map exists, and \(D\not\to E\) if none exists. Homomorphisms need not be injective. Empty relations and repeated coordinates in a tuple are allowed.

An input structure \(I\) has domain \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\geq0\), and explicitly listed relation tuples. Fix the following binary encoding. Write \(n\) as the unary prefix \(1^n0\). In signature order, write the number \(t_i\) of listed tuples of relation \(i\) as \(1^{t_i}0\), followed by its tuples in their listed order. Encode each coordinate \(v\) by \(1^{|w|}0w\), where \(w\) is the binary expansion of \(v\) without leading zeros and \(1\leq v\leq n\). Each tuple has exactly \(r_i\) coordinates. Duplicate tuples are permitted in the encoding and denote the same relation member; their bits still count. The input ends after the last relation list, with no trailing bits. Thus \(L\), the length of the entire encoding, accounts for the domain as well as all constraints. The empty-domain structure is valid only with all lists empty and is a yes instance. Any encoding polynomial-time equivalent to this explicit representation gives the same question.

For a fixed pair, define \(Y_{A,B}=\{I:I\to A\}\) and \(N_{A,B}=\{I:I\not\to B\}\). The assumption \(A\to B\) makes these sets disjoint. A valid decision algorithm accepts every input in \(Y_{A,B}\) and rejects every input in \(N_{A,B}\). It may give either answer when \(I\to B\) but \(I\not\to A\). Polynomial time means a single deterministic multitape Turing machine with a finite program, no advice or oracle, halting on every binary input of length \(L\) within \(C(L+1)^k\) steps for some fixed positive integers \(C,k\). It returns reject on malformed encodings; even instances outside the promise must obey the time bound. Reading, writing and manipulating bits all count. The constants and machine may depend on \(A,B\) and their signature, but not on \(I\).

NP-hardness here means that one uniform deterministic polynomial-time map sends every 3-CNF formula \(\varphi\) to a valid input structure \(I_\varphi\) and satisfies
\[\varphi\text{ satisfiable}\Rightarrow I_\varphi\to A,\qquad
\varphi\text{ unsatisfiable}\Rightarrow I_\varphi\not\to B.\]
A 3-CNF formula is a finite conjunction of clauses, each the disjunction of three signed Boolean variables; repeated variables and literals are allowed. For definiteness, encode its number of clauses in unary followed by three literals per clause, each a sign bit and a positive variable index encoded by the same length-prefixed binary convention as coordinates above. A positive literal is true when its variable is 1, and a negative literal when its variable is 0. The reduction's bound is polynomial in the entire formula encoding, including the time and bits needed to output \(I_\varphi\). Malformed formula encodings may map to the empty input structure. Both satisfiable and unsatisfiable formulas must map into the promise.

The question is the inclusive disjunction of these two possibilities for each fixed pair; it assumes neither \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\) nor that the alternatives are disjoint. It does not request an algorithm that, given template tables, identifies the alternative, nor a common polynomial bound over all pairs. Producing a \(B\)-valued homomorphism on every input promised to map to \(A\) is the separate search task. Counting assignments, weighted objectives, allowing a fraction of violated constraints and robustness to broken promises are not part of this decision problem.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a complete, mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the stated dichotomy for every fixed finite pair, or of its logical negation. A negative answer must establish a fixed finite signature and pair \(A\to B\) whose decision promise problem admits neither any qualifying deterministic polynomial-time decider nor any qualifying polynomial-time many-one reduction from 3-SAT. Both failures must be proved; a presently unclassified pair is not a counterexample. The positive answer need not effectively classify templates, but must establish the full quantified disjunction without an unproved complexity assumption. A dichotomy only for a restricted family, a conditional general classification, or a theorem only about the search task does not settle this target.
cards.status_note: An open general classification question in the 2022 survey and the published July 2026 Krokhin–Vagnozzi article. The latter resolves a restricted three-element target family; the May 2026 Promise MMSNP preprint gives a logical correspondence and a conditional monochromatic-clique classification. Bounded checks through 14 September 2026 found no full unconditional finite-pair dichotomy or counterexample. Individual theorem statements and scopes were checked, but their full proofs were not independently verified.

cards.title: Bodirsky–Pinsker conjecture
cards.formal:
For every countable finitely bounded homogeneous relational structure \(A\) over a finite signature, and every first-order reduct \(B\) of \(A\) with a finite relational signature, is
\[\operatorname{CSP}(B)\in\mathrm P\quad\lor\quad\operatorname{CSP}(B)\text{ is NP-complete}\ ?\]
NP-completeness uses deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. The templates are fixed before the finite input is supplied. This is the unconditional complexity dichotomy, without requiring an algebraic criterion identifying the two sides.
cards.definitions:
A finite relational signature is a finite list of relation symbols, each with a fixed positive integer arity. A structure \(D\) interprets an \(r\)-ary symbol as a subset \(R^D\subseteq D^r\) of tuples over its domain. Countable means finite or countably infinite. Empty domains, if admitted, have trivial CSPs and do not affect the question. Nullary relations can likewise be processed separately.

The induced substructure on a subset \(S\) of a domain restricts every relation to tuples from \(S\). An embedding is an injective map \(e:D\to E\) with \(\bar d\in R^D\) if and only if \(e(\bar d)\in R^E\) for every relation and tuple; it preserves both presence and absence of relation tuples. An isomorphism is a bijective embedding, and an automorphism is an isomorphism from a structure to itself. The structure \(A\) is homogeneous when every isomorphism between two finite induced substructures extends to an automorphism of \(A\).

The structure \(A\) is finitely bounded when there is a finite list \(\mathcal N\) of finite structures in its signature such that, for every finite structure \(D\) in that signature,
\[D\text{ embeds into }A\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{no }N\in\mathcal N\text{ embeds into }D.\]
Thus the finite patterns occurring inside \(A\) are precisely those avoiding finitely many forbidden induced patterns. Homogeneity is an additional condition, not part of finite boundedness alone.

A first-order reduct \(B\) has the same domain as \(A\). Each of its finitely many relations is defined by a fixed first-order formula over the relations of \(A\) and logical equality, using Boolean connectives and quantifiers over elements of \(A\), without naming parameters. It may forget original relations and introduce newly definable ones. Both signatures, \(A,B\), the defining formulas and a finite bound list witnessing the hypothesis are fixed; none is an input to the individual CSP.

An input \(I\) has finite domain \([n]\), \(n\geq0\), and an explicit list of tuples for each relation in the signature of \(B\). A homomorphism \(h:I\to B\) is any map such that \((i_1,\ldots,i_r)\in R^I\) implies \((h(i_1),\ldots,h(i_r))\in R^B\). It need not be injective and need not preserve absence of tuples. The decision problem accepts exactly when such a map exists. Repeated coordinates and isolated input elements are allowed; duplicate listed tuples are harmless. The empty input has the empty homomorphism.

Encode \(n\) in unary and each relation by a unary list length followed by binary tuple coordinates, in fixed signature order, with delimiters. Let \(L\) be total bit length. Invalid encodings are rejected. Polynomial time means a deterministic multitape Turing machine halts correctly on every input within \(C(L+1)^k\) bit steps for constants \(C,k\) depending on \(B\). No randomness, infinite-domain oracle, advice, supplied homomorphism, common polynomial exponent or algorithm choosing the correct side from template descriptions is required.

The class \(\mathrm{NP}\) consists of languages with polynomial-length certificates checkable in deterministic polynomial time. A problem \(Q\) is NP-hard under the stated reductions when, for every \(K\in\mathrm{NP}\), a total deterministic polynomial-time function \(f\) satisfies \(x\in K\) if and only if \(f(x)\in Q\). NP-complete means NP-hard and in NP. Every CSP in the displayed scope is already known to be in NP. The two alternatives are not required to be disjoint without a separation assumption: if \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), every such problem satisfies the first alternative.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed proposition, or of its logical negation, retaining every permitted structure and reduct. A negative answer must establish one permitted \(A,B\) for which \(\operatorname{CSP}(B)\) is neither in P nor NP-complete under the stated many-one reductions; membership in NP already follows from the hypotheses. No separation assumption is added to the proposition. A classification for one reduct family, the first-order/logarithmic-space-hard boundary, or a procedure deciding an algebraic meta-problem does not prove the full dichotomy. The stronger algebraic tractability conjecture would suffice if proved, but is not substituted for the existing bare complexity target.

cards.title: Word equations with linear length constraints
cards.formal: Is there a Turing machine that halts on every finite input consisting of a system of word equations \(U_{i}=V_{i}\) and a system of integer linear equalities and inequalities on the variable lengths, and answers YES exactly when a simultaneous solution exists in the free monoid \(\Sigma\)*? The alphabet, equations, variables, and arithmetic coefficients are part of the input, with the conventions below.
cards.definitions: \(\Sigma\) is a finite nonempty alphabet of constant symbols and \(X=\{X_{1},\ldots ,X_{k}\}\) is a disjoint finite set of variables. Each \(U_{i},V_{i}\) is an explicitly written finite word over \(\Sigma \cup X\); repeated occurrences of a variable must receive the same substitution. A solution assigns a finite word \(\sigma (X_{j})\in \Sigma\)* to each variable and extends by concatenation while fixing every letter of \(\Sigma\). The empty word is allowed. Every substituted equality \(\sigma (U_{i})=\sigma (V_{i})\) must hold as a literal equality of words. The additional constraints are a finite conjunction of atoms \(\sum _{j} a_{j}|\sigma (X_{j})|\le b\) or \(\sum _{j} a_{j}|\sigma (X_{j})|=b\), where all coefficients and constants are signed binary integers. Length is the number of alphabet symbols. There is no product of two variable lengths, letter-frequency counter, regular-expression predicate, string-to-integer conversion, or universal quantifier. The requested decider need not run in polynomial, elementary, or any specified computable time bound, but must terminate on satisfiable and unsatisfiable inputs alike. Nonempty-substitution requirements can be imposed using |\(\sigma (X_{j})|\ge 1\). In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.
cards.status_note: Checked through 10 September 2026. The IJCAR 2026 primary source explicitly leaves general word-equation satisfiability with length constraints open. The two-variable quadratic theorem is a restricted case, and the July NEXP-hardness claim is a lower bound rather than a decidability result. This card fixes existential satisfiability with concatenation and integer linear length constraints only.

cards.title: Decidability of unification in the basic modal logic K
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that halts on every finite modal formula \(\varphi\) and decides whether there exists a substitution \(\sigma\) for its propositional variables such that \(\sigma (\varphi )\) is valid on every Kripke frame?
cards.definitions: Formulas are finite expressions generated by variables \(p_{i} (i\in \mathbb{N} ), \perp\), negation, conjunction and the unary operator □; other Boolean connectives and ◇ are abbreviations. Variable indices use binary notation and formulas are supplied as fully written syntax trees. A substitution assigns a finite formula to each variable occurring in \(\varphi\), may use new propositional variables, and extends simultaneously through the connectives and □; it does not substitute recursively inside its newly inserted formulas. There are no distinguished parameters that must remain unchanged. A frame is a nonempty set W with an arbitrary relation \(R\subseteq \mathrm{W}\times \mathrm{W}\), finite or infinite. A valuation assigns a subset of W to every variable. Satisfaction uses the usual truth tables, ⊥ is false everywhere, and \(w\models\)□\(\psi\) iff \(v\models \psi\) for all v with wRv. Validity means satisfaction at every world in every frame with every valuation. This is the basic normal modal logic K, with no reflexivity, transitivity or seriality requirement on R. The substitution is existentially quantified without a length bound. Only its existence is decided; no running-time bound or output unifier is required. Malformed formula encodings are rejected.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a total decision procedure correct for every finite formula in the stated language, or prove that no such Turing machine exists. The unbounded substitution and arbitrary-frame semantics must remain those of parameter-free, single-modality K.
cards.status_note: Checked through 11 September 2026. No decision procedure or undecidability theorem for this exact basic-K problem was located. Beklemishev’s 2025 introduction explicitly states it as open. Nullary unification type, undecidability with extra modalities and 2025 decidability for K5 extensions do not settle it.

notes: Defined finite parameter-free simultaneous substitutions and validity over arbitrary Kripke frames.

cards.title: FO model checking on hereditary monadically dependent graph classes
cards.area: Database theory and finite model theory
cards.formal: For every hereditary effectively monadically dependent class C of finite simple graphs, do there exist a deterministic algorithm \(A_{C}, a\) computable function \(f_{C}:N\to N\) and a constant \(d_{C}\) such that \(A_{C}\) decides whether G satisfies a first-order sentence \(\varphi\) in time \(f_{C}(|\varphi |)(|V(G)|+1)^{d_{C}}\) for every \(G\in C\)? The precise effectiveness condition is given below; the graph is supplied without a structural decomposition.
cards.definitions: The class C is fixed, is closed under isomorphism and induced subgraphs, and is not part of each input. First-order sentences use equality, adjacency \(E(x,y)\), Boolean connectives and quantifiers over individual vertices. They do not quantify over sets, and no vertex order or arithmetic is supplied. The input is the explicitly represented graph G and the sentence \(\varphi\); the parameter \(k=|\varphi |\) is its encoded length. The algorithm must halt on every input, and its correctness and stated time bound are required when \(G\in C\); it need not recognize membership in C. To define monadic dependence, let \(\theta (x,y)\) be any fixed first-order formula using adjacency and finitely many additional unary predicates. A graph in \(T_{\theta}(G)\) is obtained by interpreting these predicates as arbitrary vertex subsets, putting an edge between distinct u,v whenever \(\theta (u,v)\) or \(\theta (v,u)\) holds, and taking any induced subgraph. C is monadically dependent when no single \(\theta\) gives all finite graphs among the outputs \(T_{\theta}(G), G\in C\). For an explicit effective version, define \(\mathrm{P}_{s}\) as the bipartite powerset graph with vertices \(a_{1},\ldots ,a_{s}\) and \(b_{S}\) for every \(S\subseteq \{1,\ldots ,s\}\), and edges \(a_{i} b_{S}\) exactly when \(i\in S\). Require a computable function \(b:N\to N_{\ge 1}\) such that, for every formula \(\theta\) and every \(G\in C, \mathrm{P}_{b(|\theta |)}\) is absent from \(T_{\theta}(G)\). Formula length includes its predicate symbols under a fixed effective encoding. This is the computable dependence-function convention of Mählmann’s Definition 12.24. The programs computing b and the eventual algorithm may depend on C; they are not extra per-instance certificates. The exponent \(d_{C}\) is independent of k. The query-evaluation problem here is for the plain graph signature; unary colours occur in the structural definition. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.
cards.status_note: Explicitly open in the July 2026 neighborhood-complexity paper. The independent-side hardness and stable-side algorithm are known; radius-one merge-width does not provide the full algorithm. This card fixes the effective dependence-function convention to require a computable FPT bound. No resolution found through 11 September 2026.

cards.title: Constant-delay conjunctive-query classification
cards.area: Database theory and finite model theory
cards.formal: Is there a total algorithm that, given any conjunctive query q with self-joins allowed, decides whether q admits enumeration of all distinct answers with \(O_{q}(N)\) preprocessing and \(O_{q}(1)\) worst-case delay on every database of size N?
cards.definitions: A query is a finite formula \(q(\bar\{x\})=\exists \bar\{y\} \land _{i} R_{i}(\bar\{z\}_{i})\), with no constants, negation, disequalities or aggregation. The head x̄ lists distinct variables; every variable occurs in a relational atom. Relation symbols have fixed positive finite arities within q and may occur repeatedly; repeated variables within atoms are allowed. Boolean queries have an empty head. A database D explicitly lists finite set-valued relations over a domain \([n]; N=1+n\)+the total number of tuple entries in these lists. Each domain identifier fits in \(O(\log (N+2))\) bits. \(q(D)\) is the set of head tuples extendible to an assignment satisfying all atoms. Fix the deterministic word-RAM convention with addition, multiplication, comparison, Boolean word operations and indirect access costing one step, words of \(O_{q}(\log (N+2))\) bits, and a polynomial address universe of initially zero cells. Accessed cells and operations are charged; no linear-space or constant-extra-space restriction is imposed. This allows direct tuple-membership tables without charging for touching every unused address. Membership in the target class means that for this fixed q there are an enumerator and constants \(C_{q},B_{q}\) whose preprocessing takes at most \(C_{q} N\) steps, whose word length is at most \(B_{q} \log _{2}(N+2)\), and whose time to the first answer, between consecutive answers, and from the last answer to termination is at most \(C_{q}\) after preprocessing. Empty output must be reported within the same delay bound. Output order is arbitrary and each tuple appears exactly once. The classifier takes q, not D, as input and must halt on every query; it has no prescribed runtime bound and need not output the enumerator. This is an explicit effective yes/no formulation of the source’s broader request for a complete tractability classification. The word instructions are random-access reads/writes, comparisons, conditional branches, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), integer quotient/remainder with nonzero divisor, bitwise Boolean operations, and shifts of a w-bit word; shifts by at least w yield zero. The constant in word length \(w=\Theta (\log  n)\) (or \(\Theta (\log  N)\) when N is the stated input size) is fixed with the algorithm. Address arithmetic has the same cost, larger integers occupy multiple words, and no instruction performs arbitrary-precision arithmetic in one step. When randomization is allowed, a fresh independent uniform w-bit word costs one operation. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

The exact target is an editorial effective formulation, with a specified RAM and permissive polynomial memory. Known negative classifications use stated fine-grained hypotheses; newer projected-query and dynamic results do not cover the whole class.

cards.title: \(1/3\)–\(2/3\) conjecture
cards.formal: For every integer \(n\ge 2\) and every partial order \(\mathrm{P}=([n],\le _{\mathrm{P}})\) that is not a total order, do there exist incomparable elements \(x,y\in [n]\) such that \(e(\mathrm{P})/3\le e_{\mathrm{P}}(x,y)\le 2e(\mathrm{P})/3\)?
cards.definitions: For an integer \(n\ge2\), write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A partial order \(\le_P\) is a reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive binary relation on \([n]\). Distinct elements \(x,y\) are incomparable if neither \(x\le_P y\) nor \(y\le_P x\); a total order has no incomparable pair. A linear extension is a bijection \(L:[n]\to[n]\) such that \(L(a)<L(b)\) whenever \(a\le_P b\) and \(a\ne b\). Let \(E(P)\) be the finite nonempty set of all linear extensions, \(e(P)=|E(P)|\), and \(e_P(x,y)=|\{L\in E(P):L(x)<L(y)\}|\). Probabilities use the uniform distribution on the entire set \(E(P)\), so \(\Pr[L(x)<L(y)]=e_P(x,y)/e(P)\). The endpoints \(1/3\) and \(2/3\) are included. The pair may depend on the full finite order; there is no algorithmic or representation restriction. In the context, width is the largest size of a set of pairwise incomparable elements, height the largest size of a totally ordered subset, and the cover graph joins \(x,y\) if one is strictly below the other with no element strictly between them. The balance constant is \(\beta(P)=\max_{x\ne y}\min\{e_P(x,y),e_P(y,x)\}/e(P)\).
cards.answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof that every finite non-total partial order has an incomparable pair with \(e(P)/3\le e_P(x,y)\le2e(P)/3\), or a complete Lean-checked refutation: a finite non-total order for which every incomparable pair violates that closed interval. All extension counts and probabilities must use the full set of linear extensions defined here.
cards.status_note: Rechecked on 13 September 2026. Aires–Kahn state the general conjecture separately from their large-width theorems; Gupta reports a finite census through fourteen elements. No unrestricted resolution was located in the bounded later-work check. Census computations and source proofs were not rerun independently.

cards.title: Extremal size of sunflower-free set families
cards.formal: For each fixed integer \(r\ge 3\), determine, up to constant factors as \(k\to \infty , S_{r}(k)\): the largest number of distinct k-element sets in a family containing no r members whose pairwise intersections are all equal, where the finite ground set is unrestricted.
cards.definitions: The r members in a sunflower must be distinct. Their common pairwise intersection is the core, and deleting it leaves pairwise disjoint petals. For each integer \(k\ge 1\), take the maximum cardinality over all sunflower-free families on arbitrary finite universes. The classical sunflower bound makes these cardinalities bounded by an integer depending only on k,r, so the maximum exists despite the unrestricted universe. No algorithm or encoding bound is imposed. The parameter r is fixed before k grows; asymptotic constants may depend on r.
cards.answer_criterion: Give functions \(f_{r}(k)\) and, for every fixed integer \(r\ge 3\), constants \(0<c_{r}\le C_{r}<\infty\) with \(c_{r} f_{r}(k)\le S_{r}(k)\le C_{r} f_{r}(k)\) for every \(k\ge 1\), absorbing finitely many small k into the constants if needed. Prove both a universal upper bound and existence of matching sunflower-free families in Lean. An exponential upper bound by itself does not determine the growth within constant factors.
cards.status_note: Source-backed open target. The source and relevant later-work search were reviewed on 11 September 2026; this is a bounded literature review, not a proof that no resolution exists.
